thread:
sre-jen: paging errors spiking on /v2/search/paged from the canary region, getting lots of 422s. paging client in 2.0 changed cursor encoding?
kevin: saw this too. started ~20:03 UTC after the 2.0.1 SDK rollout to canary pool A.
maria: incident-bot just paged me via on-call, forwarding logs.
incident-bot: ALERT: pager duty trigger - high error rate on /v2/search/paged (canary-a). Error class: ValidationError / cursor_parse_failed.
kevin: stack trace points to cursor.jsonDecode in client lib. Old cursors were base64, new ones expect urlsafe base64. mismatch -> parse error.
carlos: which customers hit it? any paying dedicateds?
sre-jen: support-elin pulled customer logs: ~8 customers on canary including 2 mid-market paying tenants. Errors started at 2035007740 UTC.
support-elin: affected customers seeing 422 on all paged endpoints; some retries end up with 400. No data loss, just failures to fetch next page.
pm-luca: sending a quick customer impact note to account leads. Please confirm mitigation plan.
kevin: immediate mitigation = flip canary feature flag 'compat_paging_v1' to true for canary pool A. That should force server to accept legacy cursor format.
maria: can we hotfix client to accept both encodings? low-risk change but takes a deploy.
sre-jen: agreed. do feature flag toggle now, then prepare rollback of SDK 2.0.1 to 1.9.7 in canary.
carlos: deploy-bot: can you toggle the flag?
deploy-bot: running flag toggle: set compat_paging_v1=true for pool=canary-a by @kevin.
kevin: toggled. monitoring...
sre-jen: error rate dropped ~95% within 45s. Good. keep it toggled while we sort the SDK.
maria: I'll cut a hotfix branch to make cursors backward compatible. small patch: try legacy decode if first parse fails.
kevin: pushing rollback plan: simple rollback of SDK distribution for canary -> replace 2.0.1 with 1.9.7 in canary package repo and restart canary workers. ETA 10m for rollout.
sre-jen: on-call handoff note: I'm owning mitigation, maria owns client patch, kevin owns canary rollback. Carlos, can you coordinate customer comms with PM Luca?
carlos: on it. sending preliminary customer note: "We've identified a client-side cursor encoding incompatibility affecting paginated responses in today's canary SDK rollout. A feature-flag mitigation is active and we are rolling back the canary release while issuing a compatibility patch."
pm-luca: ack. prep for postmortem item: better cross-check on wire-format invariants for paging before ship.
sre-jen: logs show one anomalous request pattern from an internal integration that used custom cursors - flag also fixed that.
support-elin: running a script to sanity-check active customer cursors and surface any that might still fail. will DM owners.
maria: uploaded quick patch branch: "compat-cursor-fallback". small change, tests added. CI green for unit tests, integration tests taking longer.
kevin: rollback to 1.9.7 in canary started. deploy-bot reporting restarts.
deploy-bot: canary-a workers rolling restart 3/12 -> 6/12 -> 12/12, progress ok.
sre-jen: monitor downstream queues, make sure no backlog. using /runbook/paging-rollout-checklist
(quoted runbook snippet)
sre-jen: ```
# paging-rollout-checklist
- toggle compat flag if break
- pause canary rollout
- rollback package
- run cursor smoke test against 5 sample tenants
- confirm no regression on embedding endpoints
```
kevin: smoke tests passed on sample tenants. metrics look healthy.
maria: creating release PR for 2.0.2 that includes fallback decoder and explicit cursor-version header. request reviews from kevin and jen.
carlos: draft customer update sent to key accounts. linking incident channel.
sre-jen: plan: keep compat_paging_v1=true in canary for 1h after rollback, then flip to false and run smoke tests. If still green, we can resume canary with 2.0.2.
pm-luca: include decision tree in postmortem: when to feature-flag vs rollback vs hotfix.
support-elin: two customers reported transient retry-induced rate-limit alarms; I'm coordinating with their SREs to clear false positives.
kevin: timecheck - mitigation took ~3m from detection to flag; rollback started at +7m; patch PR ready at +15m. good tempo.
sre-jen: tagging incident for a postmortem. severity: Sev2 (partial customer impact, mitigated quickly). assign owners and timeline.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #INC-20350 paging-protocol-drift. Severity: Sev2. Owner: sre-jen.
carlos: final note for channel: feature flag mitigated customer impact, rolling revert completed. will coordinate next steps for 2.0.2 release cadence.
sre-jen: closing thread for now, keeping monitoring open til +1h. DM me if you see any regression. :thumbsup:
